fact: The New Times opinion piece (a legal adviser at Andersen) states that Rwanda's Data Protection Act was introduced on 15 October 2021 and that its two-year grace period ended on 15 October 2023, marking the transition to enforcement and accountability.

The article states that NCSA has registered data controllers and processors (registration certificates), trained over 100 public sector Data Protection Officers and run sector workshops for pharmacists and local government entities over the last four years; it names no sanction or decision. The article gives no date for these events, so its published date of 2026-01-26 is used.

The article states that the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) acts as the supervisory authority for personal data protection and privacy under the Data Protection Act, as Rwanda observed Data Privacy Week on 26-30 January 2026.
The African Union's status list of 2 February 2026 records that Rwanda ratified or acceded to the Malabo Convention on 2019-11-14 and deposited its instrument on 2019-11-21.

CIPESA states that Rwanda's AI policy positions the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) to oversee data protection compliance relevant to AI systems; the document gives no date for this, so the published date 2026-07-23 is used.
The document names the National Cyber Security Authority (NCSA) as the Supervisory Authority under Rwanda's Law No 058/2021 and has it receive breach reports and settle disputes under that law.

NCSA's Data Protection and Privacy Office published template standard contractual clauses for transfers abroad under Article 49 of Law No 058/2021, which also set 72-hour breach reporting to the authority.
Digital Policy Alert says Rwanda implemented its personal data protection law in October 2021.
